author: assistant (claude-opus-5), M2 P2.22
constraints: n is between 2 and 10^4. Times and intervals are positive integers. The graph is connected and holds no self-loops or repeated edges.
edge_cases: The second smallest time is strictly greater than the smallest; two routes taking equal time count once between them.
input_semantics: Four parameters: n, the number of nodes labelled 1 to n; edges, a list of node pairs; time, the time to cross one edge; and change, the interval at which the signals switch.
load_bearing: Departure is permitted only during an allowing interval, so waiting time is part of the total. The value reported is the SECOND smallest distinct total time.
output_semantics: A single integer: the second smallest achievable total time.
required_operation: Every edge of an undirected graph takes the same time to cross. Signals at every node alternate between allowing and blocking departure on a fixed repeating cycle, and a traveller arriving while departure is blocked waits until it is allowed. Find the second smallest total time in which the first node can reach the last node, and report it.
source_basis: The question title and the boilerplate method name, both from this project's own bank. The bank stores NO problem description — its content field holds a placeholder and a generic example — so the behaviour described here comes from the assistant's own knowledge of the canonical task. No sentence is copied from any external problem statement.
title: Second Minimum Time to Reach Destination
